entries.prompt:
Generate one original scientific educational illustration for a Biology 30 lesson: a human trilaminar embryonic disc after gastrulation, around week 3 after fertilization. This is a schematic learning model, not a photograph or microscopy evidence.

Purpose: make the three germ layers spatially understandable without implying that human gastrulation is a spherical ball folding inward. Show one shallow oval disc in a clean oblique cutaway view, with three thin cellular sheets clearly visible at its cut edge. Ectoderm is the upper blue sheet facing the amniotic space; mesoderm is the middle muted coral sheet; definitive endoderm is the lower gold sheet facing the yolk-sac space. Keep the scale explicitly schematic: no formed fetus, limbs, organs, placenta, umbilical cord or neural tube. The sheets should look like living epithelial/cellular tissue, with restrained scientific detail, not stacked stone, fabric, food or a decorative landscape. Do not show a hole passing through all three layers or a gastric cavity inside a hollow ball. Do not claim an origin from the trophoblast or hypoblast.

Composition: wide 1536 by 1024, pale neutral background, centred disc with generous margins, uncluttered textbook illustration and clear edges. Exactly five permitted labels with thin unambiguous leader lines: “Amniotic side”, “Ectoderm”, “Mesoderm”, “Definitive endoderm”, “Yolk-sac side”. Amniotic side points to the space above the upper surface; yolk-sac side points below the lower surface. Each layer label points to only its matching coloured sheet. No other words, title, legend, numbered stages, logos, watermark or decorative arrows. Leave room below for an HTML caption authored separately. Generate the image now.

entries.prompt:
Generate one NEW original scientific educational anatomy illustration for a Biology 30 lesson, separate from the previous female and embryonic figures. Show a simplified adult human male reproductive system in a left-facing side cutaway. This is an isolated textbook anatomical schematic, not a photograph or a patient.

The purpose is to recognize the anatomical transport route and accessory glands. Show one testis inside the scrotal pouch, with the epididymis closely following the back of that testis. The vas deferens must continue from the epididymis upward into the pelvis, curve around the upper/back region of the urinary bladder, and join a short duct from the seminal vesicle behind the bladder to form an ejaculatory duct. That short ejaculatory duct passes through the prostate below the bladder and opens into the urethra. The urethra continues from the bladder through the prostate and along the penis to its exterior opening. Show the seminal vesicle as a small lobulated gland behind the bladder, not as the bladder itself. Show one small bulbourethral gland below the prostate near the base of the penis, with its short duct joining the urethra. Paired reproductive structures are represented by one side for clarity. Keep all duct junctions traceable; the vas deferens must not empty into the bladder. Keep the urethra visibly continuous and separate from the vas deferens. A pale bladder is included only as a position landmark.

Exactly ten allowed labels, with thin unambiguous leader lines pointing to the correct tissue or duct: “Testis”, “Epididymis”, “Vas deferens”, “Seminal vesicle”, “Ejaculatory duct”, “Prostate”, “Bulbourethral gland”, “Urethra”, “Penis”, “Scrotum”. Do not label the bladder or add any other words. Label the epididymis on its coiled duct, scrotum on the outer pouch, testis on the organ inside, and urethra on the internal passage rather than the penis surface. No functional claims inside labels. Use restrained natural tissue shading with distinct duct outlines, generous pale background margins, large readable dark labels outside the anatomy and no leader-line collisions. Wide 1536 by 1024. No person, face, rectum, bowel, bones, erection, sexual activity, semen, sperm cells, flow arrows, instruments, surgery, title, logo or watermark. Keep the whole non-erect anatomical schematic inside the frame. Generate the illustration now.

revisions.prompt:
Revise this male reproductive anatomy image to fix one crucial duct connection. The vas deferens currently appears to connect to the upper head region of the epididymis, leaving the lower tail as a dead end. This is incorrect for teaching the transport route.

The epididymis must have a head at the upper pole of the testis, a coiled body along its posterior side, and a tail at the LOWER pole. The coiled tail must visibly continue directly into the vas deferens at the bottom of the testis. From that lower-tail connection, the vas must turn upward and ascend behind/beside the testis into the pelvis. Remove any connection between the ascending vas and the upper epididymal head. Make the tail-to-vas junction unmistakable, and keep the three-dimensional layering simple enough to trace it. Do not add a new duct from the testis straight to the vas. Keep the epididymis leader on its coiled body.

Retain the route of the vas around the bladder and its union with the seminal-vesicle duct to form the ejaculatory duct, which passes through the prostate into the urethra. Keep the continuous urethra and bulbourethral gland connection. Remove the unexplained upright reddish tube behind the seminal vesicle because that extra urinary landmark is outside the intended illustration. Preserve the ten existing labels, generous margins and non-erect isolated textbook side view. No new labels, arrows, captions, logos or other elements. Generate the corrected image now.

entries.prompt:
Generate one NEW original educational scientific illustration for Biology 30: two isolated tissue cross-sections comparing a growing ovarian follicle before ovulation with the corpus luteum after ovulation. This is a simplified explanatory schematic, not a photograph, medical scan or microscopy evidence.

LEFT PANEL: a growing antral follicle with a surrounding wall of supporting cells, a large clear fluid-filled antrum, and ONE large round oocyte embedded in a mound of supporting cells attached to the inner follicle wall. The oocyte must not float freely in the middle of the fluid-filled space. Show the oocyte as one cell with a simple nucleus, visibly distinct from the many smaller supporting cells. Do not specify an exact meiotic stage.

RIGHT PANEL: corpus luteum as thick folded glandular tissue derived from the follicular tissue remaining after ovulation. No oocyte inside this structure. A small irregular central space is acceptable, but do not draw another large follicle with a retained egg. No arrow from the oocyte to the corpus luteum; no fertilization or embryo.

Use exactly these six labels: left heading “Growing follicle”; left leaders “Oocyte”, “Supporting cells”, “Fluid-filled space”; right heading “Corpus luteum”; right subheading “After ovulation”. The Oocyte leader ends inside the single large cell, Supporting cells points to a small-cell cluster around it, and Fluid-filled space points into the clear antrum. Thin distinct leaders, no collisions, large readable dark text. No other words, logos, watermark, arrows or decorative elements. Wide 1536 by 1024, pale neutral background, ample margins, restrained textbook-style tissue colours and clean cellular detail. Relative sizes and colours are schematic. Generate the image now.
